# {{projectName}} — OpenAPI SDK Generation

Generate client SDKs from the API's OpenAPI spec and publish them to
their package registries. Two targets exist today — TypeScript
(`typescript-fetch`, web/Next.js) and Dart (`dart-dio`, Flutter) — and
the setup is built to take more.

## Run on request only

Only do this work when the user asks for it. Ask which targets to
generate — do not assume both. Each target is generated separately via
`--generator-key`.

## Step 0 — tool check

Verify the tools for the *requested* targets before generating. If any
are missing, suggest the install and stop — do not attempt generation.

| Tool | Needed for | Check | Install hint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Java 17+ JRE | generator CLI wraps the Java jar | `java -version` | `winget install EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.17.JRE` |
| Node.js + npx | runs `openapi-generator-cli` | `node --version` | `winget install OpenJS.NodeJS.LTS` |
| pnpm | TS SDK install + build | `pnpm --version` | `npm i -g pnpm` |
| Dart SDK | Dart SDK build + publish | `dart --version` | `winget install Dart.DartSDK` |

## 1. Source of truth

The OpenAPI spec is the single contract for every client SDK. Changes
always flow: **spec → regenerate SDK → publish**. Generated output is
never hand-edited — it is regenerated wholesale, and it IS committed
under `sdks/` so diffs show exactly what a spec change did to each
client.

### Emitting the spec

`{{projectName}}.Api` produces the spec at **runtime** via
Swashbuckle.AspNetCore: `AddSwaggerGen` registers `SwaggerDoc("v1")`
and `Program.cs` calls `UseSwagger()` in Development only. There is no
checked-in spec and no build-time emitter — run the API and download
the document:

```bash
docker compose up -d db   # Program.cs runs migrations at startup
dotnet run --project {{projectName}}.Api   # Development environment
curl -sf http://localhost:<port>/swagger/v1/swagger.json -o openapi.json
```

`<port>` is whatever the API binds to (launchSettings / console
output; the docker-compose api service maps 8080). Keep `openapi.json`
at the repo root — `openapitools.json` points `inputSpec` at it. It is
a build artifact: regenerating it is expected, hand-editing it is not.

## 2. Generator config

One `openapitools.json` at the repo root pins `generator-cli.version`
— never float it. Output shape changes between generator releases;
bump the version deliberately, regenerate every target, and review the
diffs. It holds one generator key per SDK target, each outputting to
`sdks/<lang>/<pkg>`:

```json
{
  "spaces": 2,
  "generator-cli": {
    "version": "7.10.0",
    "generators": {
      "sdks/ts/<pkg>": {
        "generatorName": "typescript-fetch",
        "output": "sdks/ts/<pkg>",
        "inputSpec": "openapi.json",
        "additionalProperties": { "...": "see section 3" }
      },
      "sdks/dart/<pkg>": {
        "generatorName": "dart-dio",
        "output": "sdks/dart/<pkg>",
        "inputSpec": "openapi.json",
        "additionalProperties": { "...": "see section 4" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Generate a single target:

```bash
npx @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli generate --generator-key <key>
```

## 3. TypeScript SDK (web / Next.js)

Generator key `sdks/ts/<pkg>` uses `typescript-fetch` with:

```json
"additionalProperties": {
  "npmName": "@marcellebond/{{projectNameLower}}-sdk",
  "npmVersion": "0.1.0",
  "npmRepository": "https://npm.pkg.github.com",
  "supportsES6": true,
  "typescriptThreePlus": true,
  "withInterfaces": true,
  "prefixParameterInterfaces": true,
  "useSingleRequestParameter": true,
  "stringEnums": true,
  "enumPropertyNaming": "original",
  "modelPropertyNaming": "camelCase",
  "paramNaming": "camelCase",
  "fileNaming": "kebab-case",
  "importFileExtension": ".js",
  "platform": "browser",
  "withoutRuntimeChecks": false,
  "ensureUniqueParams": true,
  "sortParamsByRequiredFlag": true,
  "sortModelPropertiesByRequiredFlag": true,
  "legacyDiscriminatorBehavior": false
}
```

Then inside `sdks/ts/<pkg>`:

```bash
pnpm install && pnpm build
```

## 4. Dart SDK (Flutter)

Generator key `sdks/dart/<pkg>` uses **`dart-dio` (not the plain `dart`
generator)** with:

```json
"additionalProperties": {
  "pubName": "<pkg>",
  "pubLibrary": "<pkg>",
  "pubVersion": "0.1.0",
  "pubDescription": "<one line>",
  "pubPublishTo": "https://onepub.dev/api/<org-id>",
  "serializationLibrary": "json_serializable",
  "enumUnknownDefaultCase": true,
  "useEnumExtension": true,
  "nullableFields": false,
  "hideGenerationTimestamp": true
}
```

Distribution is **OnePub** (private pub registry — GitHub Packages has
no pub support, and `git:`/`path:` deps are banned in Flutter
consumers). The generated models need a **mandatory** `build_runner`
pass inside `sdks/dart/<pkg>` or they do not compile:

```bash
dart pub get && dart run build_runner build -d && dart format .
```

## 5. Versioning

SDK version == API release version. Tagging the API `v1.2.3` publishes
SDKs at `1.2.3` so every consumer pin maps to one contract version.
CI injects the tag into `npmVersion` and `pubVersion` via
`--additional-properties` — never bump the hand-maintained value in
`openapitools.json` for a release.

## 6. Publishing

**TypeScript → GitHub Packages.** `npmName` under `@marcellebond`,
registry `https://npm.pkg.github.com`, auth via a PAT with
`write:packages` stored as the `GITHUB_PACKAGES_PUBLISH_TOKEN` repo
secret — never committed. The SDK's `.npmrc` needs the matching
scope mapping:

```
@marcellebond:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com
//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}
```

**Dart → OnePub** via the `pubPublishTo` baked into the pubspec.
`dart pub publish` authenticates with a token delivered as an env var:

```bash
dart pub token add https://onepub.dev/api/<org-id> \
  --env-var ONEPUB_TOKEN
dart pub publish --force
```

`ONEPUB_TOKEN` is a repo secret produced locally by `onepub export`.
Never commit the token.

## 7. CI — `.github/workflows/sdk.yml`

Runs on `v*` tags: emit spec → TS generate/install/build/publish →
Dart generate/pub get/build_runner/format/token/publish. Pinned action
versions, minimal permissions:

```yaml
name: sdk
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write

jobs:
  publish-sdks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      VERSION: ${{ github.ref_name }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with: { distribution: temurin, java-version: "17" }
      - uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v4
        with: { dotnet-version: "10.0.x" }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: "22" }
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1

      - name: Emit OpenAPI spec
        run: |
          docker compose up -d db
          cd {{projectName}}.Api
          ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development \
            nohup dotnet run --urls http://localhost:8080 \
            > api.log 2>&1 &
          for i in $(seq 1 60); do
            curl -sf http://localhost:8080/swagger/v1/swagger.json \
              -o "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/openapi.json" && exit 0
            sleep 2
          done
          cat api.log
          exit 1

      - name: Generate TypeScript SDK
        run: |
          npx @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli generate \
            --generator-key sdks/ts/<pkg> \
            --additional-properties npmVersion=${VERSION#v}

      - name: Build and publish TypeScript SDK
        working-directory: sdks/ts/<pkg>
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_PACKAGES_PUBLISH_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          pnpm install
          pnpm build
          printf '%s\n' \
            "@marcellebond:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com" \
            "//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}" \
            > .npmrc
          pnpm publish --no-git-checks

      - name: Generate Dart SDK
        run: |
          npx @openapitools/openapi-generator-cli generate \
            --generator-key sdks/dart/<pkg> \
            --additional-properties pubVersion=${VERSION#v}

      - name: Build and publish Dart SDK
        working-directory: sdks/dart/<pkg>
        env:
          ONEPUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ONEPUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          dart pub get
          dart run build_runner build -d
          dart format .
          dart pub token add https://onepub.dev/api/<org-id> \
            --env-var ONEPUB_TOKEN
          dart pub publish --force
```

## 8. Consumer contract

**Next.js** installs the package pinned exactly (no `^`) and iterates
locally via **yalc** — never commit `file:`/`link:` deps:

```json
"dependencies": {
  "@marcellebond/{{projectNameLower}}-sdk": "1.2.3"
}
```

**Flutter** apps depend on the hosted `^version` in `pubspec.yaml`.
Local iteration uses a sibling checkout via a `dependency_overrides`
entry in `pubspec_overrides.yaml` (gitignored, personal — never
committed):

```yaml
dependency_overrides:
  <pkg>:
    path: ../<api-repo>/sdks/dart/<pkg>
```

The committed `pubspec.yaml` must never contain a `path:` dep for a
published package. Flutter consumers inject their own configured `Dio`
into the generated client — they do not wrap generated models.

## 9. Adding another SDK target

1. Add a `sdks/<lang>/<pkg>` generator key with its
   `additionalProperties` to `openapitools.json`.
2. Document the target's required post-generation build step in this
   skill (Dart's is `build_runner`; find the equivalent for the new
   generator before running it).
3. Add matching generate/build/publish steps to `sdk.yml` and its
   registry auth to the secrets list.
